subject: [PATCH v5 0/12] mm: fix allocator races with memory hotplug

reviews.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: The author is addressing a concern that the zonelist_update_seq retry should not be limited to CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE, as this can cause spurious allocation failures for __GFP_THISNODE callers when onlining zones. The author agrees and explains that build_zonerefs_node() rewrites the zonelists in place, shifting entries in every zonelist containing a zone being onlined.
reviews.raw_body:
Commit 2c4c3e29897d ("mm/page_alloc: simplify __alloc_pages_slowpath()
flow") retries an allocation once with reserve_flags when the caller
becomes eligible for reserves, guarded by can_retry_reserves.

A restart after a cpuset update or a zonelist rebuild retries with
can_retry_reserves already set to false, so a caller that cannot
reclaim (GFP_NOWAIT | __GFP_MEMALLOC), fails without trying reserves.

Reset can_retry_reserves on restart. Only a cpuset or zonelist change
restarts the slowpath, so the retry still runs at most once per change.

With a kprobe helping to make the race deterministic, an allocation
can be made to return NULL. With this patch the allocation will succeed.

Fixes: 2c4c3e29897d ("mm/page_alloc: simplify __alloc_pages_slowpath() flow")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 mm/page_alloc.c | 3 ++-
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/mm/page_alloc.c b/mm/page_alloc.c
index a8cac5e01066..f1048168c90c 100644
--- a/mm/page_alloc.c
+++ b/mm/page_alloc.c
@@ -4783,7 +4783,7 @@ __alloc_pages_slowpath(gfp_t gfp_mask, unsigned int order,
 	unsigned int zonelist_iter_cookie;
 	int reserve_flags;
 	bool compact_first = false;
-	bool can_retry_reserves = true;
+	bool can_retry_reserves;
 	unsigned long alloc_start_time = jiffies;
 
 	if (unlikely(nofail)) {
@@ -4805,6 +4805,7 @@ __alloc_pages_slowpath(gfp_t gfp_mask, unsigned int order,
 	no_progress_loops = 0;
 	compact_result = COMPACT_SKIPPED;
 	compact_priority = DEF_COMPACT_PRIORITY;
+	can_retry_reserves = true;
 	cpuset_mems_cookie = read_mems_allowed_begin();
 	zonelist_iter_cookie = zonelist_iter_begin();
 
-- 
2.56.0

---

From: Josef Bacik <josef@toxicpanda.com>

should_reclaim_retry() walks a zonelist and passes the zoneref pointer
to the reclaim_retry_zone tracepoint, which loads the zone from the
entry again to find the node.

Memory hotplug rebuilds the zonelists in place while allocations are
under way. When a zone in front of the zoneref entry has become empty,
the entries move up, and this one can be the end marker by the time the
tracepoint looks at it. zonelist_node_idx() then dereferences a NULL
zone. Short of that, the event can name another zone than the one its
numbers belong to.

Pass the zone pointer instead of the zoneref pointer.

Fixes: d379f01de095 ("oom, trace: add oom detection tracepoints")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Assisted-by: LLM
Signed-off-by: Josef Bacik <josef@toxicpanda.com>
Signed-off-by: David Hildenbrand (Arm) <david@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Vlastimil Babka (SUSE) <vbabka@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 include/trace/events/oom.h | 8 ++++----
 mm/page_alloc.c            | 2 +-
 2 files changed, 5 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)

diff --git a/include/trace/events/oom.h b/include/trace/events/oom.h
index 9f0a5d1482c4..cbcf6fe4cc61 100644
--- a/include/trace/events/oom.h
+++ b/include/trace/events/oom.h
@@ -33,7 +33,7 @@ TRACE_EVENT(oom_score_adj_update,
 
 TRACE_EVENT(reclaim_retry_zone,
 
-	TP_PROTO(struct zoneref *zoneref,
+	TP_PROTO(struct zone *zone,
 		int order,
 		unsigned long reclaimable,
 		unsigned long available,
@@ -41,7 +41,7 @@ TRACE_EVENT(reclaim_retry_zone,
 		int no_progress_loops,
 		bool wmark_check),
 
-	TP_ARGS(zoneref, order, reclaimable, available, min_wmark, no_progress_loops, wmark_check),
+	TP_ARGS(zone, order, reclaimable, available, min_wmark, no_progress_loops, wmark_check),
 
 	TP_STRUCT__entry(
 		__field(	int, node)
@@ -55,8 +55,8 @@ TRACE_EVENT(reclaim_retry_zone,
 	),
 
 	TP_fast_assign(
-		__entry->node = zonelist_node_idx(zoneref);
-		__entry->zone_idx = zonelist_zone_idx(zoneref);
+		__entry->node = zone_to_nid(zone);
+		__entry->zone_idx = zone_idx(zone);
 		__entry->order = order;
 		__entry->reclaimable = reclaimable;
 		__entry->available = available;
diff --git a/mm/page_alloc.c b/mm/page_alloc.c
index 1850a41f24f7..e14d550d4128 100644
--- a/mm/page_alloc.c
+++ b/mm/page_alloc.c
@@ -4670,7 +4670,7 @@ should_reclaim_retry(gfp_t gfp_mask, unsigned order,
 		 */
 		wmark = __zone_watermark_ok(zone, order, min_wmark,
 				ac->highest_zoneidx, alloc_flags, available);
-		trace_reclaim_retry_zone(z, order, reclaimable,
+		trace_reclaim_retry_zone(zone, order, reclaimable,
 				available, min_wmark, *no_progress_loops, wmark);
 		if (wmark) {
 			ret = true;
-- 
2.56.0

---

The zonelist_update_seq retry was limited to CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE,
presumably because only hot-remove takes zones out of a zonelist.

However, build_zonerefs_node() rewrites the zonelists in place, so
onlining the first block of a zone shifts the entries that follow it
in every zonelist containing that zone.  This can cause a spurious
allocation failure for a __GFP_THISNODE caller.

For a node with only ZONE_NORMAL, onlining its first ZONE_MOVABLE block
rewrites the node's ZONELIST_NOFALLBACK list as:

  [NORMAL, NULL] -> [MOVABLE, NULL] -> [MOVABLE, NORMAL, NULL]

A concurrent GFP_KERNEL | __GFP_THISNODE allocation can observe the
intermediate list, skip ZONE_MOVABLE, and find no eligible zone. With
CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE=n, check_retry_zonelist() returns 0 and the
allocation fails even though the node has free ZONE_NORMAL memory.

Gate the sequence checks on CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTPLUG, which covers every
configuration that rebuilds zonelists after boot.

Fixes: 3d36424b3b58 ("mm/page_alloc: fix race condition between build_all_zonelists and page allocation")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reviewed-by: Vlastimil Babka (SUSE) <vbabka@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 mm/page_alloc.c | 4 ++--
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/mm/page_alloc.c b/mm/page_alloc.c
index e14d550d4128..11be12b443ad 100644
--- a/mm/page_alloc.c
+++ b/mm/page_alloc.c
@@ -4404,7 +4404,7 @@ static DEFINE_SEQLOCK(zonelist_update_seq);
 
 static unsigned int zonelist_iter_begin(void)
 {
-	if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE))
+	if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTPLUG))
 		return read_seqbegin(&zonelist_update_seq);
 
 	return 0;
@@ -4412,7 +4412,7 @@ static unsigned int zonelist_iter_begin(void)
 
 static unsigned int check_retry_zonelist(unsigned int seq)
 {
-	if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE))
+	if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTPLUG))
 		return read_seqretry(&zonelist_update_seq, seq);
 
 	return seq;
-- 
2.56.0

---

From: Josef Bacik <josef@toxicpanda.com>

When the last memory of a zone goes offline, zone_pcp_reset() frees
zone->per_cpu_pageset and zone->per_cpu_zonestats. Nothing waits for those
who found the zone populated and still use the two pointers. They take
neither the memory hotplug lock nor any other lock which offline_pages()
holds, and some of them can sleep:

  CPU0 vmstat_update()                CPU1 offline_pages()
  refresh_cpu_vm_stats()
    for_each_populated_zone(zone)
      pcp = zone->per_cpu_pageset
      cond_resched()
                                      adjust_present_page_count()
                                      zone_pcp_reset(zone)
                                        free_percpu(zone->per_cpu_pageset)
      decay_pcp_high(zone, pcp)
      __this_cpu_write(pcp->expire, 0)

The same goes for drain_all_pages(NULL), which takes pcp->lock, for
zone_pcp_update(), show_free_areas() and the readers and writers of the
zonestats. If the per-cpu memory has got a new owner in the meantime, it
is corrupted.

The pagesets are only freed because setup_zone_pageset() would otherwise
leak them when the zone gets memory again. Keep them instead and let
setup_zone_pageset() and zone_pcp_init() use them again, like it is done
with pgdat->per_cpu_nodestats. Their lists are empty, and their limits
have been calculated for a zone without memory by the
init_per_zone_wmark_min() of offline_pages(), which is what
setup_zone_pageset() would come up with as well.

Fixes: 340175b7d14d ("mm/hotplug: free zone->pageset when a zone becomes empty")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Assisted-by: LLM
Signed-off-by: Josef Bacik <josef@toxicpanda.com>
Signed-off-by: David Hildenbrand (Arm) <david@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Johannes Weiner <hannes@cmpxchg.org>
Signed-off-by: Vlastimil Babka (SUSE) <vbabka@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 mm/page_alloc.c | 20 ++++++++++++++------
 1 file changed, 14 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)

diff --git a/mm/page_alloc.c b/mm/page_alloc.c
index f1048168c90c..1850a41f24f7 100644
--- a/mm/page_alloc.c
+++ b/mm/page_alloc.c
@@ -6308,6 +6308,10 @@ void __meminit setup_zone_pageset(struct zone *zone)
 {
 	int cpu;
 
+	/* The zone has been populated before, see zone_pcp_reset(). */
+	if (zone->per_cpu_pageset != &boot_pageset)
+		return;
+
 	/* Size may be 0 on !SMP && !NUMA */
 	if (sizeof(struct per_cpu_zonestat) > 0)
 		zone->per_cpu_zonestats = alloc_percpu(struct per_cpu_zonestat);
@@ -6400,6 +6404,10 @@ void __init setup_per_cpu_pageset(void)
 
 __meminit void zone_pcp_init(struct zone *zone)
 {
+	/* A node which is added again, see zone_pcp_reset(). */
+	if (zone->per_cpu_pageset && zone->per_cpu_pageset != &boot_pageset)
+		return;
+
 	/*
 	 * per cpu subsystem is not up at this point. The following code
 	 * relies on the ability of the linker to provide the
@@ -7680,6 +7688,12 @@ void zone_pcp_enable(struct zone *zone)
 	mutex_unlock(&pcp_batch_high_lock);
 }
 
+/*
+ * The zone has become empty. Its pagesets and zonestats are not freed: nothing
+ * keeps somebody who found the zone populated, such as refresh_cpu_vm_stats()
+ * or drain_all_pages(), from still using them. They are used again when the
+ * zone gets memory again.
+ */
 void zone_pcp_reset(struct zone *zone)
 {
 	int cpu;
@@ -7690,12 +7704,6 @@ void zone_pcp_reset(struct zone *zone)
 			pzstats = per_cpu_ptr(zone->per_cpu_zonestats, cpu);
 			drain_zonestat(zone, pzstats);
 		}
-		free_percpu(zone->per_cpu_pageset);
-		zone->per_cpu_pageset = &boot_pageset;
-		if (zone->per_cpu_zonestats != &boot_zonestats) {
-			free_percpu(zone->per_cpu_zonestats);
-			zone->per_cpu_zonestats = &boot_zonestats;
-		}
 	}
 }
 
-- 
2.56.0

---

Memory hotplug rebuilds zonelists in place while allocations walk them,
so a zoneref slot can change between two loads of it.

zonelist_zone() loads the slot with a plain access.  The compiler may
load it again later instead of keeping the zone it already read, so a
caller can check one zone and then use another, or the NULL terminator.

Use READ_ONCE().  Callers that take a zone from a slot and keep using
it, such as get_page_from_freelist() with ac->preferred_zoneref, need
that single load.

Fixes: 11cd8638c37f ("mm, page_alloc: remove stop_machine from build_all_zonelists")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 include/linux/mmzone.h | 3 ++-
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/include/linux/mmzone.h b/include/linux/mmzone.h
index ecd1ebd49756..4bc2318ac37f 100644
--- a/include/linux/mmzone.h
+++ b/include/linux/mmzone.h
@@ -1855,7 +1855,8 @@ extern struct zone *next_zone(struct zone *zone);
 
 static inline struct zone *zonelist_zone(struct zoneref *zoneref)
 {
-	return zoneref->zone;
+	/* Memory hotplug rewrites zonelists in place. */
+	return READ_ONCE(zoneref->zone);
 }
 
 static inline int zonelist_zone_idx(const struct zoneref *zoneref)
-- 
2.56.0

---

__next_zones_zonelist() tests a slot's zone for NULL, then reads the
slot again to look up the zone's node. Offlining a zone's last block
rebuilds the zonelists in place, so the second read can return the
terminator:

  CPU 0                             CPU 1
  __next_zones_zonelist(nodemask)
    zonelist_zone(slot 1) = NORMAL
                                    offline_pages()
                                      build_all_zonelists()
                                        [MOVABLE, NORMAL, NULL]
                                        -> [NORMAL, NULL]
    zref_in_nodemask(slot 1)
      zone_to_nid(NULL)

Current GCC and clang merge the two reads, but nothing requires it.
With mm/mmzone.o built with -fno-inline -fno-ipa-sra, holding a
nodemask allocation between the reads while the node's last movable
block goes offline oopses every time:

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000060
  RIP: 0010:zone_to_nid+0x0/0x10
  Call Trace:
   zref_in_nodemask+0x9/0x20
   __next_zones_zonelist+0x23/0x70
   prepare_alloc_pages.constprop.0+0x16c/0x190
   __alloc_frozen_pages_noprof+0xaf/0x330

Read the slot once and test that zone. A NULL zone still ends the walk.

Fixes: 11cd8638c37f ("mm, page_alloc: remove stop_machine from build_all_zonelists")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
Reviewed-by: Vlastimil Babka (SUSE) <vbabka@kernel.org>
---
 mm/mmzone.c | 11 ++++++-----
 1 file changed, 6 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)

diff --git a/mm/mmzone.c b/mm/mmzone.c
index 9cc9ef588580..65880396f104 100644
--- a/mm/mmzone.c
+++ b/mm/mmzone.c
@@ -43,13 +43,14 @@ struct zone *next_zone(struct zone *zone)
 	return zone;
 }
 
-static inline int zref_in_nodemask(struct zoneref *zref,
-				   const nodemask_t *nodes)
+/* A NULL zone terminates the zonelist, so it ends the search. */
+static inline bool zone_in_nodemask(const struct zone *zone,
+				    const nodemask_t *nodes)
 {
 #ifdef CONFIG_NUMA
-	return node_isset(zonelist_node_idx(zref), *nodes);
+	return !zone || node_isset(zone_to_nid(zone), *nodes);
 #else
-	return 1;
+	return true;
 #endif /* CONFIG_NUMA */
 }
 
@@ -67,7 +68,7 @@ struct zoneref *__next_zones_zonelist(struct zoneref *z,
 			z++;
 	else
 		while (zonelist_zone_idx(z) > highest_zoneidx ||
-				(zonelist_zone(z) && !zref_in_nodemask(z, nodes)))
+		       !zone_in_nodemask(zonelist_zone(z), nodes))
 			z++;
 
 	return z;
-- 
2.56.0

---

Onlining the first block of a zone rebuilds every zonelist in place,
shifting the slots after the new zone.  The iterator approves a slot,
then the allocator loads the zone from it, so a GFP_KERNEL request can
land in ZONE_MOVABLE and a nodemask request on a node outside its mask:

  CPU 0                             CPU 1
  prepare_alloc_pages()
    first_zones_zonelist(nodemask {1})
      slot 0 (NORMAL1) approved
                                    online_pages()
                                      build_all_zonelists()
                                        [NORMAL1, NORMAL2, ...]
                                        -> [MOVABLE1, NORMAL1, ...]
  get_page_from_freelist()
    zone = zonelist_zone(slot 0)    /* MOVABLE1 */
    allocates from MOVABLE1

zonelist_update_seq detects the rebuild, but only the slowpath's failure
exits check it.

Check it whenever an allocation succeeds too, and if it changed, free
the page and retry, as the memcg charge failure path does.  Eligible
pages are dropped as well: zonelists only change when memory comes or
goes, and a retry is simpler than rechecking the page.

Freeing the page does not undo a block the allocation claimed.  A
GFP_KERNEL request that lands in a fresh ZONE_MOVABLE converts a free
block to MIGRATE_UNMOVABLE, which stays until the zone's movable free
list runs out and a movable allocation takes it back.

The fast and bulk paths read the seqlock's raw seqcount without waiting:
an ALLOC_NOLOCK caller can be an NMI that interrupted the writer, and on
PREEMPT_RT the seqlock accessor takes the spinlock.  A sample taken
mid-write costs a retry, or NULL under ALLOC_NOLOCK.
check_retry_zonelist() returns 0 when compiled out, so a backport
without the hot-add change stays harmless.

Fixes: 11cd8638c37f ("mm, page_alloc: remove stop_machine from build_all_zonelists")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
Reviewed-by: Vlastimil Babka (SUSE) <vbabka@kernel.org>
---
 mm/page_alloc.c | 34 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++-
 1 file changed, 33 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/mm/page_alloc.c b/mm/page_alloc.c
index 28d46f987685..f2f7e96bdef2 100644
--- a/mm/page_alloc.c
+++ b/mm/page_alloc.c
@@ -4419,12 +4419,25 @@ static unsigned int zonelist_iter_begin(void)
 	return 0;
 }
 
+/*
+ * Never wait for the writer, which an ALLOC_NOLOCK caller in NMI may have
+ * interrupted. Read the raw seqcount: on PREEMPT_RT the seqlock accessor takes
+ * the spinlock while a write is in progress.
+ */
+static unsigned int zonelist_iter_sample(void)
+{
+	if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTPLUG))
+		return raw_seqcount_begin(&zonelist_update_seq.seqcount.seqcount);
+
+	return 0;
+}
+
 static unsigned int check_retry_zonelist(unsigned int seq)
 {
 	if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTPLUG))
 		return read_seqretry(&zonelist_update_seq, seq);
 
-	return seq;
+	return 0;
 }
 
 /* Perform direct synchronous page reclaim */
@@ -5100,6 +5113,12 @@ __alloc_pages_slowpath(gfp_t gfp_mask, unsigned int order,
 	warn_alloc(gfp_mask, ac->nodemask,
 			"page allocation failure: order:%u", order);
 got_pg:
+	/* A rebuild during the walk may have handed out an ineligible zone. */
+	if (page && check_retry_zonelist(zonelist_iter_cookie)) {
+		__free_frozen_pages(page, order, FPI_NONE);
+		page = NULL;
+		goto restart;
+	}
 	return page;
 }
 
@@ -5184,6 +5203,7 @@ unsigned long alloc_pages_bulk_noprof(gfp_t gfp, int preferred_nid,
 	struct list_head *pcp_list;
 	struct alloc_context ac;
 	unsigned int alloc_flags = ALLOC_WMARK_LOW;
+	unsigned int zonelist_iter_cookie;
 	int nr_populated = 0, nr_account = 0;
 
 	/*
@@ -5224,6 +5244,7 @@ unsigned long alloc_pages_bulk_noprof(gfp_t gfp, int preferred_nid,
 	/* May set ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT, fragmentation will return 1 page. */
 	gfp &= gfp_allowed_mask;
 	gfp = current_gfp_context(gfp);
+	zonelist_iter_cookie = zonelist_iter_sample();
 	if (!prepare_alloc_pages(gfp, 0, preferred_nid, nodemask, &ac, &gfp, &alloc_flags))
 		goto out;
 
@@ -5273,6 +5294,10 @@ unsigned long alloc_pages_bulk_noprof(gfp_t gfp, int preferred_nid,
 	if (unlikely(!zone))
 		goto failed;
 
+	/* The zone was chosen from a zonelist that a rebuild may have changed. */
+	if (unlikely(check_retry_zonelist(zonelist_iter_cookie)))
+		goto failed;
+
 	/* spin_trylock may fail due to a parallel drain or IRQ reentrancy. */
 	pcp = pcp_spin_trylock(zone->per_cpu_pageset);
 	if (!pcp)
@@ -5413,6 +5438,7 @@ struct page *__alloc_frozen_pages_noprof(gfp_t gfp, unsigned int order,
 		.alloc_flags = alloc_flags,
 	};
 	unsigned int fastpath_alloc_flags = alloc_flags;
+	unsigned int zonelist_iter_cookie;
 
 	/* Other flags could be supported later if needed. */
 	if (WARN_ON(alloc_flags & ~(ALLOC_NOLOCK | ALLOC_NO_CODETAG)))
@@ -5442,6 +5468,7 @@ struct page *__alloc_frozen_pages_noprof(gfp_t gfp, unsigned int order,
 	 */
 	gfp = current_gfp_context(gfp);
 	alloc_gfp = gfp;
+	zonelist_iter_cookie = zonelist_iter_sample();
 	if (!prepare_alloc_pages(gfp, order, preferred_nid, nodemask, &ac,
 			&alloc_gfp, &fastpath_alloc_flags))
 		return NULL;
@@ -5458,6 +5485,11 @@ struct page *__alloc_frozen_pages_noprof(gfp_t gfp, unsigned int order,
 
 	/* First allocation attempt (or, for nolock, only attempt) */
 	page = get_page_from_freelist(alloc_gfp, order, fastpath_alloc_flags, &ac);
+	if (likely(page) && unlikely(check_retry_zonelist(zonelist_iter_cookie))) {
+		__free_frozen_pages(page, order,
+				    alloc_flags & ALLOC_NOLOCK ? FPI_NOLOCK : 0);
+		page = NULL;
+	}
 	if (likely(page) || (alloc_flags & ALLOC_NOLOCK))
 		goto out;
 
-- 
2.56.0

reviews.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about the dequeue_hugetlb_folio_nodemask() function, which can take a pool page from another node due to a rebuild of the zonelist. The author added checks for zonelist updates and restarts the walk if it changed. This change fixes a fault bound to one node taking a page from another in 3 out of 3 runs with kprobes holding the walk across the online.

2026-10-31.patch_summary: This patch series addresses memory hotplug-related races and issues in the Linux kernel's memory allocator. The patches fix problems such as zone list rebuilds, page set freeing, and allocation failures that can occur when memory is added or removed from a system while allocations are happening. The approach taken involves fixing specific walkers and functions to ensure correct behavior during these operations, including removing a helper function that invites the same bug. The patches were tested on a QEMU guest with three NUMA nodes and showed improved results compared to an unmodified kernel.

reviews.author: Vlastimil (SUSE)
reviews.summary: Reviewer Vlastimil (SUSE) noted that patch 5, which makes zonelist_zone() read the slot once using READ_ONCE(), is missing a lock drop before calling try_to_unmap(). This creates a lock ordering violation with reclaim paths.
reviews.raw_body:
On 11/1/26 03:13, Gregory Price (Meta) wrote:
> Memory hotplug rebuilds zonelists in place while allocations walk them,
> and offlining an emptied zone frees pagesets the vmstat worker can still
> hold.
> 
> These eleven fixes cover the walkers that crash, fail, or pick the wrong
> zone or node as a result, and a twelfth patch removes a helper that
> invites the same bug.
> 
>    1. a restarted slowpath loses its retry with reserves
>    2. offlining an emptied zone frees pagesets still in use
>    3. the reclaim_retry_zone tracepoint rereads a zoneref slot
>    4. the zonelist retry is compiled out without MEMORY_HOTREMOVE
>    5. zonelist_zone() may load its slot more than once
>    6. NULL preferred zone after a shrink rebuild
>    7. __next_zones_zonelist() rereads a slot
>    8. allocations land outside their zone or nodemask
>    9. the hugetlb pool walk takes another node's page
>   10. alloc_contig_pages() takes a range outside its filters
>   11. mempolicy_slab_node() rereads a slot
>   12. zonelist_node_idx() invites the same double read
>

On Sat Oct 31, 2026 at 10:13 PM EDT, Gregory Price (Meta) wrote:
> Commit 2c4c3e29897d ("mm/page_alloc: simplify __alloc_pages_slowpath()
> flow") retries an allocation once with reserve_flags when the caller
> becomes eligible for reserves, guarded by can_retry_reserves.
>
> A restart after a cpuset update or a zonelist rebuild retries with
> can_retry_reserves already set to false, so a caller that cannot
> reclaim (GFP_NOWAIT | __GFP_MEMALLOC), fails without trying reserves.
>
> Reset can_retry_reserves on restart. Only a cpuset or zonelist change
> restarts the slowpath, so the retry still runs at most once per change.
>
> With a kprobe helping to make the race deterministic, an allocation
> can be made to return NULL. With this patch the allocation will succeed.
>

On Sat Oct 31, 2026 at 10:13 PM EDT, Gregory Price (Meta) wrote:
> The zonelist_update_seq retry was limited to CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE,
> presumably because only hot-remove takes zones out of a zonelist.
>
> However, build_zonerefs_node() rewrites the zonelists in place, so
> onlining the first block of a zone shifts the entries that follow it
> in every zonelist containing that zone.  This can cause a spurious
> allocation failure for a __GFP_THISNODE caller.
>
> For a node with only ZONE_NORMAL, onlining its first ZONE_MOVABLE block
> rewrites the node's ZONELIST_NOFALLBACK list as:
>
>   [NORMAL, NULL] -> [MOVABLE, NULL] -> [MOVABLE, NORMAL, NULL]
>
> A concurrent GFP_KERNEL | __GFP_THISNODE allocation can observe the
> intermediate list, skip ZONE_MOVABLE, and find no eligible zone. With
> CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE=n, check_retry_zonelist() returns 0 and the
> allocation fails even though the node has free ZONE_NORMAL memory.
>
> Gate the sequence checks on CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTPLUG, which covers every
> configuration that rebuilds zonelists after boot.
>

2026-11-01.patch_summary: This patch series addresses memory hotplug-related races and issues in the Linux kernel's memory allocator. The patches fix problems such as zone list rebuilds, page set freeing, and allocation failures that can occur when memory is added or removed from a system while allocations are happening. The approach taken involves fixing specific walkers and functions to ensure correct behavior during these operations, including removing a helper function that invites the same bug. The patches were tested on a QEMU guest with three NUMA nodes and showed improved results compared to an unmodified kernel.
